Building UI tests extends what you already know about XCTest and unit tests: create a UI test target, classes, and methods, then use XCTest assertions to verify expectations. It exposes semantic information describing how to interact with the App. Integrated into UIKit and APPKit, it provides APIs for adjusting behavior and exposing functionality; UI tests use this information. Creating UI tests in source resembles creating unit tests. Add a UI test target to the app; Xcode creates a test group and implementation file containing method templates. You can specify the application to test when creating the target. UI tests find interface objects through queries, synthesize events, and dispatch them to those objects. APIs let tests inspect properties and states and compare them with expected values.
